articles.title: Para-cyclist Shaik Arshad fractures leg in fall; medical support missing
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Para-cyclist Shaik Arshad suffered multiple fractures to his previously operated left residual limb after a fall during the men’s time trial at
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Para-cyclist Shaik Arshad suffered multiple fractures to his previously operated left residual limb after a fall during the men’s time trial at the Asian Para Games in Japan on Wednesday, raising questions over the absence of dedicated medical support for the Indian team.Sources told TOI that Arshad, a 2024 Paralympian, crashed in heavy rain at the Izu Velodrome in Shizuoka, sustaining serious injuries to the above-knee amputated limb on which he relies to use his prosthesis. He requires urgent medical attention and surgery, with concerns over the implications for his future mobility.The cycling venue is more than 250 km from Nagoya. Sources said officials had initially asked Arshad and his support staff to travel to Nagoya for hospital admission. Following prolonged discussions, officials agreed to visit the competition venue, where the injured cyclist needed immediate attention.The incident has also raised questions about assurances regarding medical arrangements for the Indian para-cycling contingent. Sources said that at a meeting on Sept 8 at the Sports Authority of India (SAI) office here, involving Arshad’s coach Aditya Verma and SAI officials from the Teams division, with Paralympic Committee of India (PCI) officials participating through phone calls, assurances were apparently given that medical personnel would accompany the team.However, no dedicated medical personnel were available to attend to Arshad at the venue when the accident occurred, sources alleged. Arshad’s coach is now exploring options to travel urgently from Hyderabad to Japan and is arranging a visa to be by the athlete’s side.The injury is particularly serious because it involves Arshad’s residual limb, which is crucial for fitting and using his artificial leg. articles.title: India's Anahat Singh stuns eight-time World Champion Nour ElSherbini at Silicon Valley Open
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Eighteen-year-old Anahat Singh of India produced one of the standout results of the 2026 PSA Squash Tour when she defeated eight-time world
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Eighteen-year-old Anahat Singh of India produced one of the standout results of the 2026 PSA Squash Tour when she defeated eight-time world champion Nour ElSherbini 11-8, 11-8, 11-7 in just 30 minutes at the Silicon Valley Open in Redwood City on Wednesday.The straight-games victory over the top-seeded Egyptian, a World No. 3 and equal of Nicol David’s record for most world titles, propelled the Indian into the quarter-finals of the USD143,500 PSA Gold event and marked the biggest win of her professional career.Singh, born in New Delhi on 13 March 2008 and currently ranked around the world top 15-17, has risen rapidly.She became India’s first World Junior champion earlier in 2026, the first non-Egyptian winner since 2010, and claimed a historic women’s singles silver at the 2026 Asian Games in Japan.Coached by former world No. 1 Grégory Gaultier alongside Saurav Ghosal and Stéphane Galifi, she turned professional in 2023 and has already collected multiple PSA titles while becoming the youngest Asian player to crack the top 20.ElSherbini, a dominant force who has held the world No. 1 ranking for extended periods and won four British Opens, arrived in California as the clear favourite.Anahat Singh enters quarterfinalsSingh, who has now qualified for the quarter-finals, had earlier eased past Nour Aboulmakarim in the opening round.After the upset she reflected that she had “grown up watching every single match” of the Egyptian, underscoring the personal weight of the result against a player she has long admired.The win arrives as squash prepares for its Olympic debut at Los Angeles 2028.For Singh, it confirms her ability to trouble the game’s established elite on the senior tour and strengthens her case for further ranking progress.The Silicon Valley Open, staged from 20-24 October, continues to showcase a new generation capable of challenging the long-standing hierarchy led by Egyptian players.Stay updated with the articles.title: WWE announces  title match for SmackDown; could have major impact on Crown Jewel 2026 card
articles.summary: WWE is only two weeks away from presenting its next Premium Live Event, Crown Jewel 2026.
articles.body: WWE is only two weeks away from presenting its next Premium Live Event, Crown Jewel 2026. However, the company has announced a major title match to take place on the upcoming episode of SmackDown. This could lead to the card for Crown Jewel being altered in a major way should the challenger emerge victorious and defeat the champion.WWE Women’s title match announced for SmackDownSmackDown General Manager Nick Aldis posted a video on X announcing that Roxanne Perez will challenge Chelsea Green for the WWE Women’s Championship. The match will take place on the upcoming October 23rd edition of Friday Night SmackDown.Why could this match's outcome have a major impact on the WWE Crown Jewel 2026 card?If the match ends with Roxanne Perez defeating Chelsea Green and becoming the new WWE Women’s Champion, she will replace her in the upcoming Champion vs. Champion match for the Crown Jewel Championship at the namesake PLE set for November 7 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Interestingly, her opponent will be none other than her Judgment Day ally, Liv Morgan, who is the reigning WWE Women’s World Champion after winning back the title from Stephanie Vaquer in a triple-threat match involving Becky Lynch at Money in the Bank 2026 PLE.How did Roxanne Perez earn the opportunity to challenge Chelsea Green for the WWE Women’s title?On the October 12 episode of RAW after Money in the Bank, Chelsea Green interrupted Liv Morgan's championship-win celebration. After a back-and-forth exchange, an impromptu non-title match was made between Green and Morgan’s ally, Roxanne Perez. Despite multiple interferences from Judgment Day, Green held her own and fought valiantly against the Prodigy. However, the numbers game proved too much for her, as a distraction led Perez to deliver a Pop Rox on Green and pick up a huge win.Therefore, she likely earned the opportunity after pinning the reigning WWE Women’s Champion in a singles match. So, Perez has an opportunity to head into the historic title match at Crown Jewel PLE, but first she needs to defeat Green one more time on the upcoming episode of SmackDown, which is expected to be an incredible showdown.Also read: 5 WWE Crown Jewel matches that were show stealers including John Cena’s classic showdownStay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
